questions.question: Explain Catford’s Linguistic Theory / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Catford's Linguistic Theory - Catford’s theory defines translation as a formal linguistic
  • substitution of text in one language by equivalent text in another, introducing key concepts like shift and
  • equivalence boundaries. It views translation strictly through a structural, linguistic lens rather than
  • communicative function.

questions.question: Describe the significance of localization in translation / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the significance of localization in translation - Localization tailors translated content to fit the
  • specific linguistic, cultural, and technical expectations of a target geographic region. It ensures that elements
  • like formats, symbols, and regional norms resonate authentically with local audiences.

questions.question: Explain why human insight matters when translating cultural content / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:

  • decode deep-seated idioms, historical subtexts, humor, and social sensitivities without causing offense.

questions.question: Explain Roman Jakobson's three-fold classification of translation using examples from the media industry. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Roman Jakobson's three-fold classification of translation using examples from the media
  • industry.
  •  Intralingual Translation (Rewording): Translating or paraphrasing within the same language, such as
  • modernizing classical news archives or adapting complex scripts for simpler broadcasts.
  •  Interlingual Translation (Proper Translation): Translating between two different natural languages, such
  • as localizing an international English news report into regional Indian languages.
  •  Intersemiotic Translation (Transmutation): Translating verbal signs into non-verbal systems, such as
  • adapting a written investigative feature article or novel into a visual film script or documentary.

questions.question: Explain the main purpose of press releases in organizational communication. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the main purpose of press releases in organizational communication.
  •  Official Information Dissemination: Serving as the formal, verified channel for corporations or
  • governments to announce news, product launches, or policy updates to media outlets.
  •  Brand Image and Narrative Control: Ensuring that organizational messages, executive quotes, and key
  • data points are communicated accurately and uniformly across public channels.
  •  Newsroom Usability: Providing structured, pre-formatted content (headline, lead, boilerplate) that
  • journalists can easily process, translate, and syndicate into public news stories.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the impact of online translation tools and Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the modern translation industry. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the impact of online translation tools and Artificial Intelligence (Al) on the modern translation
  • industry.
  •  Speed and Efficiency: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) and AI models process massive volumes of text
  • instantly, drastically cutting down production time and costs for global media distribution.
  •  Workflow Evolution (PEMTs): Shifting human roles from scratch-translation to Post-Editing Machine
  • Translation (PEMTs), where humans refine raw AI outputs for cultural nuance and tone.
  •  Limitations and Risks: Highlighting AI's struggle with sarcasm, deep cultural context, and idiomatic humor,
  • alongside data privacy risks when handling confidential corporate translations.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Prepare a detailed essay on the core elements of creative writing / [CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Prepare a detailed essay on the core elements of creative writing
  •  Plot and Structure: The logical sequence of events, frameworks (like the Three-Act structure), and
  • narrative arcs that provide momentum and direction to a story.
  •  Characterization and Voice: Crafting multi-dimensional figures with distinct psychological depths,
  • motivations, and establishing a unique authorial tone or acoustic identity.
  •  Setting, Conflict, and Theme: Using sensory descriptions to build atmospheric worlds, introducing central
  • struggles to generate tension, and communicating the underlying philosophical message.
